newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Chinese trade says tin price too low for exports.
newsitem.headline: Chinese trade says tin price too low for exports.

text.p: Chinese tin traders are unlikely to export tin despite the rise in LME prices, a Chinese trader said on Wednesday.

"They would like the price to be at about US$6,300 per tonne to make exports viable since domestic prices are still quite high," the trader said at the China non-ferrous metal fair being held this week in Hong Kong.
The LME tin prices went up about US$100 last night, the trader said. "It's good news but it's still too low," he said, adding that tin prices had been wallowing at low levels since May 1996.
London Metal Exchange (LME) three-month tin closed $90 a tonne higher on Tuesday at $5,970 after meeting resistance at the psychological $6,000 level.

The tin market was well supported, initially by a $280-tonne stocks fall, but also by narrowing spreads. Cash/threes, around a $40 contango on Monday, contracted to around $10 at one point before being indicated at $7/17.

In the Chinese domestic market tin is indicated around 50,000 yuan, or about US$6,024 a tonne, but local interest rates of between 12-13 percent can push the domestic price up to around $6,320 compared to an LME CIF Rotterdam price of about
"We keep it in our hands, paying interest and warehouse charges and wait for the price to go up," the trader said, adding the warehouse charges are 0.5 yuan per day per tonne.
"The whole non-ferrous metal market has been very dour for a long time," he said.
Yunnan is one of China's biggest tin producing provinces. The Yunnan Tin Corporation produces LME registered YT brand tin for export.
Yuannan exports tin to the Rotterdam LME warehouse, to Japan and Taiwan.
